001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.json.encoder;
002
003import static io.jstach.rainbowgum.json.JsonBuffer.EXTENDED_F;
004
005import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
006import java.time.Instant;
007import java.time.format.DateTimeFormatterBuilder;
008import java.util.Map;
009import java.util.Objects;
010import java.util.function.Consumer;
011
012import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
013
014import io.jstach.rainbowgum.KeyValues;
015import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEncoder;
016import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogEvent;
017import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.LevelFormatter;
018import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.ThrowableFormatter;
019import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogFormatter.TimestampFormatter;
020import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProperties;
021import io.jstach.rainbowgum.LogProvider;
022import io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation.LogConfigurable;
023import io.jstach.rainbowgum.json.JsonBuffer;
024import io.jstach.rainbowgum.json.JsonBuffer.ExtendedFieldPrefix;
025import io.jstach.rainbowgum.json.JsonBuffer.JSONToken;
026
027/**
028 * A JSON encoder in
029 * <a href="https://go2docs.graylog.org/5-2/getting_in_log_data/gelf.html">GELF JSON
030 * format</a>.
031 */
032public final class GelfEncoder extends LogEncoder.AbstractEncoder<JsonBuffer> {
033
034        /**
035         * GELF encoder URI scheme.
036         */
037        public static final String GELF_SCHEME = "gelf";
038
039        private final String host;
040
041        private final KeyValues headers;
042
043        private final boolean prettyPrint;
044
045        /**
046         * Default number of fractional second digits the <code>_time</code> field is rendered
047         * with, see {@link #of(String, String, Map, Boolean, Integer, Integer)}.
048         */
049        public static final int DEFAULT_TIME_FRACTIONAL_DIGITS = 3;
050
051        private final TimestampFormatter timeFormatter;
052
053        private final int maxBufferSize;
054
055        GelfEncoder(String host, KeyValues headers, boolean prettyPrint, int timeFractionalDigits, int maxBufferSize) {
056                super();
057                this.host = host;
058                this.headers = headers;
059                this.prettyPrint = prettyPrint;
060                this.timeFormatter = timeFormatter(timeFractionalDigits);
061                this.maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize;
062        }
063
064        /*
065         * GELF's own "timestamp" field (a UNIX epoch double, see doEncode) is always
066         * millisecond precision by construction (derived from Instant.toEpochMilli()), so it
067         * needs no formatter and is unaffected by this. "_time" is a RainbowGum-only extra
068         * field giving a human-readable ISO-8601 instant alongside it - unlike "timestamp",
069         * Instant.now() on most JVMs has real nanosecond resolution, so formatting it with
070         * DateTimeFormatter.ISO_INSTANT (variable-width, 0-9 fractional digits depending on
071         * the actual instant) is both needlessly precise for a log timestamp and, because a
072         * fresh format() call happens on every single event, needlessly expensive. Fixing the
073         * width to timeFractionalDigits makes the output caching-safe the same way
074         * DefaultInstantFormatter.ISO's fix did (see LogFormatter/PatternFormatterFactory) -
075         * caching only kicks in at millisecond-or-coarser precision (<=3 digits), since finer
076         * precision genuinely varies within the same millisecond.
077         */
078        private static TimestampFormatter timeFormatter(int fractionalDigits) {
079                if (fractionalDigits < 0 || fractionalDigits > 9) {
080                        throw new IllegalArgumentException(
081                                        "timeFractionalDigits must be between 0 and 9 inclusive: " + fractionalDigits);
082                }
083                var dtf = new DateTimeFormatterBuilder().appendInstant(fractionalDigits).toFormatter();
084                return TimestampFormatter.of(dtf, fractionalDigits <= 3);
085        }
086
087        /**
088         * Creates a GELF encoder using a lambda for easier registration. The builder will
089         * have properties loaded after the consumer has configured the builder.
090         * @param consumer lambda to configure builder.
091         * @return GELF encoder provider.
092         */
093        public static LogProvider<GelfEncoder> of(Consumer<GelfEncoderBuilder> consumer) {
094                return (s, c) -> {
095                        var b = new GelfEncoderBuilder(s);
096                        consumer.accept(b);
097                        return b.fromProperties(c.properties()).build();
098                };
099        }
100
101        /**
102         * Creates GELF Encoder.
103         * @param name property name prefix.
104         * @param host host field in GELF.
105         * @param headers additional headers that will be prefix with "_".
106         * @param prettyPrint <code>true</code> will pretty print the JSON, default is false.
107         * @param timeFractionalDigits number of fractional second digits (0-9) the
108         * non-standard <code>_time</code> field is rendered with, default
109         * {@value #DEFAULT_TIME_FRACTIONAL_DIGITS} (milliseconds). Values above 3 render
110         * genuine sub-millisecond precision (most JVMs' {@link Instant#now()} has real
111         * nanosecond resolution) but cannot be cached the way millisecond-or-coarser
112         * precision can, since it can legitimately differ between two events in the same
113         * millisecond.
114         * @param maxBufferSize maximum buffer size - a soft ceiling checked between events,
115         * not a hard cap enforced on any single event (see
116         * {@link LogEncoder.Buffer#isOversized()}). A negative value (the default) disables
117         * this entirely.
118         * @return encoder.
119         */
120        @LogConfigurable(prefix = LogProperties.ENCODER_PREFIX)
121        static GelfEncoder of(@LogConfigurable.KeyParameter String name, String host, //
122                        @Nullable Map<String, String> headers, //
123                        @Nullable Boolean prettyPrint, @Nullable Integer timeFractionalDigits, @Nullable Integer maxBufferSize) {
124                prettyPrint = prettyPrint == null ? false : prettyPrint;
125                Objects.requireNonNull(host);
126                var _headers = KeyValues.of(headers == null ? Map.of() : headers);
127                int _timeFractionalDigits = timeFractionalDigits == null ? DEFAULT_TIME_FRACTIONAL_DIGITS
128                                : timeFractionalDigits;
129                int _maxBufferSize = maxBufferSize == null ? -1 : maxBufferSize;
130
131                return new GelfEncoder(host, _headers, prettyPrint, _timeFractionalDigits, _maxBufferSize);
132        }
133
134        @Override
135        protected JsonBuffer doBuffer(BufferHints hints) {
136                return new JsonBuffer(this.prettyPrint, ExtendedFieldPrefix.UNDERSCORE, maxBufferSize);
137        }
138
139        @Override
140        protected void doEncode(LogEvent event, JsonBuffer buffer) {
141                buffer.clear();
142                var formattedMessage = buffer.getFormattedMessageBuilder();
143                final String host = this.host;
144                event.formattedMessage(formattedMessage);
145                final String shortMessage = formattedMessage.toString();
146                Instant now = event.timestamp();
147                final double timeStamp = ((double) now.toEpochMilli()) / 1000;
148                @Nullable String fullMessage = null;
149                var t = event.throwableOrNull();
150                if (t != null) {
151                        formattedMessage.append("\n");
152                        ThrowableFormatter.appendThrowable(formattedMessage, t);
153                        fullMessage = formattedMessage.toString();
154                }
155                int level = levelToSyslogLevel(event.level());
156                buffer.write(JSONToken.OBJECT_START);
157                int index = 0;
158                index = buffer.write("host", host, index);
159                index = buffer.write("short_message", shortMessage, index);
160                index = buffer.write("full_message", fullMessage, index);
161                index = buffer.writeDouble("timestamp", timeStamp, index, 0);
162                index = buffer.writeInt("level", level, index, 0);
163                StringBuilder timeBuilder = new StringBuilder(32);
164                timeFormatter.formatTimestamp(timeBuilder, now);
165                index = buffer.write("_time", timeBuilder.toString(), index);
166                index = buffer.write("_level", LevelFormatter.toString(event.level()), index);
167                index = buffer.write("_logger", event.loggerName(), index);
168                index = buffer.write("_thread_name", event.threadName(), index);
169                index = buffer.write("_thread_id", String.valueOf(event.threadId()), index);
170
171                if (t != null) {
172                        String tn = t.getClass().getName();
173                        index = buffer.write("_throwable", tn, index);
174                }
175
176                var kvs = event.keyValues();
177
178                /*
179                 * output headers
180                 */
181                index = headers.forEach((src, k, v, idx, buf) -> {
182                        if (kvs.getValueOrNull(k) != null) {
183                                return idx;
184                        }
185                        return buf.write(k, v, idx, EXTENDED_F);
186                }, index, buffer);
187
188                /*
189                 * output MDC
190                 */
191                index = kvs.forEach((src, k, v, idx, buf) -> buf.write(k, v, idx, EXTENDED_F), index, buffer);
192
193                index = buffer.write("version", "1.1", index);
194
195                if (index > 0 && prettyPrint) {
196                        buffer.writeLineFeed();
197                }
198                buffer.write(JSONToken.OBJECT_END);
199                buffer.writeLineFeed();
200        }
201
202        private int levelToSyslogLevel(Level level) {
203                /*
204                 * FROM LOGBACK The syslog severity of a logging event is converted from the level
205                 * of the logging event. The DEBUG level is converted to 7, INFO is converted to
206                 * 6, WARN is converted to 4 and ERROR is converted to 3.
207                 */
208                int r = switch (level) {
209                        case ERROR -> 3;
210                        case DEBUG -> 7;
211                        case INFO -> 6;
212                        case TRACE -> 7;
213                        case WARNING -> 4;
214                        case ALL -> 7;
215                        case OFF -> 0;
216                };
217                return r;
218        }
219
220}
